### Observed differences

- In the later window, A43 appears in about 70 in 100 traces, up from about 58 in 100 in the earlier window, and its mean number of executions per trace rises from about 0.8 to about 1.0. [OCC041, POS002]
- A42 is present in every trace in both windows and is executed more often per trace in the later window (about 1.8 versus about 1.6 executions), while its relative position in the case is essentially unchanged (mean event position about 0.85 in both windows). [OCC040, POS001]
- A42 and A43 co-occur in about 70 in 100 traces in the later window versus about 58 in 100 before; traces with A42 but without A43 fall from about 43 to about 30 in 100, the interleaved-or-repeated share among joint traces rises from about 30 to about 38 in 100, and A43 never appears without A42 in either window. [REL001]
- Successor shares shift toward the A42–A43 exchanges: from A42, the share of outgoing transitions to A43 rises from about 48% to 56% while the share to A44 falls from about 51% to 43%; from A43, the share back to A42 rises from about 38% to 43% while the share to A46 falls from about 62% to 53%; from A45, the share to A42 rises from about 37% to about 43%. [DIR042, DIR043, DIR045]
- The strictly consecutive A43-then-A42 succession becomes relatively less common: among A43→A42 pairs within five steps, the share at distance 1 falls from about 42% to about 33%. [LAG003]
- In one branch region, A01, A05, A07 and A09 each appear in fewer traces in the later window (about 48–51 in 100, down from about 56–58 in 100), while A03, A11, A12 and A13 each appear in more (about 52 in 100, up from about 44 in 100). [OCC001, OCC003, OCC005, OCC007, OCC009, OCC011, OCC012, OCC013]
- In the A31–A38 region, A35 and A36 each appear in about 41–42 in 100 traces (down from about 50–51 in 100) while A37 and A38 appear in about 58–59 in 100 (up from about 50 in 100), and several successor shares rotate (for example, from A31 the share to A38 rises from about 23% to 32% while the share to A36 falls from about 28% to 17%). [OCC033, OCC034, OCC035, OCC036, DIR031, DIR035, DIR036, DIR037, DIR038]
- Smaller shifts: A24 appears in more traces (about 55 versus 47 in 100) with A21 routing more to A24 (about 20% to 29% of its outgoing transitions) and A23 appearing in fewer traces (about 47 versus 53 in 100); from A40, the share to A41 rises from about 61% to 70% while the share to A39 falls, and A39 appears in fewer traces (about 13 in 100, on small support). [OCC023, OCC024, DIR021, DIR040, OCC037]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, cases run through A43 more often and repeat the interplay between A42 and A43 more intensively: A43 participates in about 70 in 100 traces versus about 58 in 100 (it occurs only alongside A42), A42 recurs more within traces (about 1.8 versus 1.6 executions per trace), and routing shares shift toward the pair (A42→A43 up from about 48% to 56% of A42's outgoing transitions, A43→A42 up from about 38% to 43%, A45→A42 up similarly). The key differences are large for 200-trace windows and almost never produced by random re-splits (empirical strengths about 0.99 for A43's participation and the co-occurrence shift, about 0.95 for the A42 routing shift), and participation, recurrence, relational and routing indicators all point the same way — although they partly describe the same traces, so they are not independent confirmations. [OCC040, OCC041, POS002, REL001, DIR042, DIR043, DIR045]

Limitations: the evidence set contains no screening baseline, so item counts cannot be compared with a chance expectation; the extra co-occurrence is not explained by strictly consecutive execution alone (the distance-1 share of A43→A42 pairs falls to about 33% even though A43→A42 rises as a share of A43's outgoing transitions), so the exact shape of the additional repetition is not pinned down; and an important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the additional A42–A43 executions are a downstream consequence of the broader redistribution of case flow visible in other regions rather than a change localised at this pair. [LAG003, DIR043, OCC007, OCC013, DIR031]

Other differences:
- A shift between two alternative branches: A01, A05, A07 and A09 appear in fewer traces while A03, A11, A12 and A13 appear in more, each moving about 6–9 cases in 100 (strengths up to about 0.93). [OCC001, OCC003, OCC005, OCC007, OCC009, OCC011, OCC012, OCC013]
- A redistribution inside the A31–A38 region: A35 and A36 appear in fewer traces, A37 and A38 in more, with several successor shares rotating (for example A31→A38 up and A31→A36 down, strength about 0.95). [OCC033, OCC034, OCC035, OCC036, DIR031, DIR035, DIR036, DIR037, DIR038]
- Smaller changes around A21–A24 (A24 up, A23 down, A21→A24 up) and around A39/A40 (A40→A41 up, A40→A39 down). [OCC023, OCC024, DIR021, DIR040, OCC037]
- Routing profiles of rarely observed sources (A02, A04, A08, A10, A47) differ strongly between the windows but rest on only about 4–18 outgoing transitions per window with low reference strength, which an unchanged process typically produces; A14–A20 and A25–A34 are essentially stable. [DIR002, DIR004, DIR008, DIR010, DIR047, OCC015, OCC016, OCC019, OCC025, OCC028, OCC031]
